what: Grid, decision rule and shape prediction for the RATE_TOL_REL sweep (#775), committed BEFORE any point is measured. The instrument is tools/probes/rate_tol_sweep.py, committed in the same change and run only afterwards; its refusal on an uncommitted or dirty plan is the temporal proof, as tools/sweep_m1a_attack.py's refusal on a dirty attack-sweep/grid.json is for that sweep.
parameter: RATE_TOL_REL in model/discrimination_features.py: the RELATIVE half of what test_extra_features_are_rate_independent is allowed to call 'the same number' at 44.1 kHz and 48 kHz. The comparison is max(RATE_TOL_REL * peak, RATE_TOL_ABS[unit]), so the dial is the relative term only and the per-unit floor is held fixed.
range_basis: 0.12 is what ships. It is on the grid so the record prices the CHANGE and not only the dial, the same reason -1 is on fold-interpolator's grid and 0 is on dphase-ar1-floor's.
0.06 and 0.03 are the first two halvings of the shipped value; the third halving, 0.015, is within 3 % of 0.0146 below and is represented by it.

0.02 = RATE_TOL_ABS['ratio'] / 1.0. max() means a pair stops responding to this dial once RATE_TOL_REL * peak falls under the unit's absolute floor, so 0.02 is the value below which the relative term can no longer bind on a correlation column saturating at +-1 -- which is every column #775 is about (jit.cyclecorr.seg0, mpd*.rowcorr.*). It is the most load-bearing point on the grid.

0.0146 is the WHOLE EFFECT jit.cyclecorr.seg0 reports between a steady 410 Hz square and the same square with 0.5 % per-period jitter (#775's headline, re-measured on this tree). A tolerance at or above the effect cannot assert a margin below it, so this is the break-even point and it is a measured row rather than an assertion.

0.00625 = RATE_TOL_ABS['db'] / 80 dB. cqt_features and multiscale_features clamp at floor_db = -80.0, so 80 dB is the largest magnitude the vector can carry; below 0.00625 no dB column responds to the dial either, and 147 of the 191 columns are dB.

0.0 removes the relative term entirely: every comparison becomes RATE_TOL_ABS[unit]. It is the endpoint whose behaviour is arithmetic rather than measurement, and it bounds what this dial can achieve at all.
held_fixed: RATE_TOL_ABS (all five per-unit floors), FOLD_SINC_TAPS at its shipped 16 for the cost panel and at -1 for the benefit panel, and the stimulus panel itself: tools/probes/fold_rate_sweep.py's 44 values of f0 in both resampling directions, plus the two control shapes RATE_PANEL carries (0.1 % jitter, band-limited square) at both build rates.
objective: caught -- the number of (panel entry, column) pairs the rate-independence comparison turns red on the INTEGER FOLD that shipped before #767, over the wide panel. Higher is better: it is how much real 44.1k<->48k dependence the control can see, measured on the honest injected defect test_the_integer_fold_this_replaced_is_still_red_on_this_panel already uses. jit.* columns are excluded on any entry where dominant_period disagrees between the two rates by more than 5 %, because the two sides are then measuring different partials (#774) and a gap read off them is not about this dial.
constraint: cost -- the same count on the SHIPPED fold, split by unit. A clean panel turning red is the price, and it must be reported per unit because the two families' floors stand in completely different relations to their columns' magnitudes (0.02 against a correlation of ~1, 0.5 dB against a cqt column clamped at -80). A single undifferentiated count would hide the distinction the decision turns on. Reported in the same artefact; the gate reads only the objective column, exactly as dphase-ar1-floor's sees_real is read by a human and not by the gate.

decision_rule.why: the objective is an INTEGER COUNT of (entry, column) pairs. Two counts are equal or they are not; there is no 'within' for a count, so the rule has to be exact equality. The wide panel is at most 92 entries x 191 columns = 17572 pairs, so any relative tolerance below 1/17572 = 5.7e-5 is exact equality by construction, and 1e-5 is below it with a factor of 5.7 to spare. Stated from the objective's own granularity and the panel's size, both known before the sweep ran, and not from the spread of the data. Tighter than the granularity is the conservative direction: a rule finer than the objective can split points the objective would call equal, which can only add groups, never manufacture a plateau.

prediction.basis: Derived from the max() and from the vector's per-unit magnitude ceilings, neither of which is a point on this sweep. (a) MONOTONE: lowering RATE_TOL_REL can only lower each pair's tolerance, so caught is non-increasing in the dial and every group is an interval. (b) A pair responds to the dial only while RATE_TOL_REL > floor/peak. The ceilings are fixed by the module: dB is clamped at floor_db = -80 so floor/peak bottoms out at 0.5/80 = 0.00625; a ratio column's largest peak on a square is 1.86 (shapevar), so 0.02/1.86 = 0.0108, and for the saturating correlations #775 is about it is 0.02/1.0 = 0.02; ms is 0.05/2.27 = 0.022; count is 1.0/102 = 0.0098 and a cycle-count gap is an integer >= 1 against a tolerance that never falls below 1.0, so it can never be red at all; ppm is 0 on every jitterless clip (the relative term is then exactly 0 and the tolerance is the 20 ppm floor), and only the two 0.1 %-jitter control entries make it live, at 20/5.7e3 = 0.0035. (c) So BELOW 0.00625 the dial is inert for every family except ppm on two of the 92 entries, where a crossing needs a 44.1k<->48k phase-scatter gap landing in the single narrow band (20, 35.6] ppm out of a quantity spanning 0.8 ppm (jitterless resampler residue, already measured in this module) to 5.7e3 ppm -- so [0.0, 0.00625] is ONE group. (d) ABOVE 0.00625 each interval opens a wide band of responding magnitudes: (0.00625, 0.0146] opens dB magnitudes 34-80, (0.0146, 0.02] opens dB 25-34 and ratio peaks 1.00-1.37 (which is exactly where the saturating rowcorr and cyclecorr columns sit), (0.02, 0.03] opens dB 17-25 and ratio 0.67-1.00, (0.03, 0.06] opens dB 8.3-17 and ratio 0.33-0.67, (0.06, 0.12] opens dB 4.2-8.3 and ratio 0.17-0.33. The panel puts 44 values of f0 in both resampling directions into each of those bands and the gaps vary continuously with f0, so each of the five intervals is predicted to hold at least one crossing: five singletons. Verdict MIXED, 6 groups over 7 points. THE WIDE PANEL IS THE SUBJECT ON PURPOSE: the 11-entry RATE_PANEL's trade was already measured during curation (tools/probes/rate_tol_feasibility.py, f46732a3 on branch curator/775-feasibility) and published in #775, so a prediction restating that is not a prediction.

what_would_falsify_it: A plateau anywhere above 0.00625 refutes (d): it would mean a whole band of magnitudes has no crossing in it on 88 entries, which is a fact about the panel's coverage and would mean the grid is too fine for what the panel can resolve.
0.0 separating from 0.00625 refutes (c): the only mechanism that permits it is a ppm crossing in (20, 35.6] on a jittered control entry, so the detail table would have to name that entry and column.
